title: Whiskey Emoji 🥃 Meaning: Tumbler Glass, Neat or on the Rocks
description: The tumbler glass 🥃 is the whiskey emoji: bourbon, scotch, a drink on the rocks or a shot. Learn how people use it for toasts, Father's Day and tough days.
summary: 🥃 is a short, heavy tumbler holding an amber drink, and most people read it as whiskey, bourbon or scotch. It means a strong drink, often sipped slowly, and is used for unwinding, toasts, gifts for whiskey lovers and shots. Like other alcohol emojis it has no hidden slang meaning.
meaning: Before this emoji arrived in 2016, whiskey drinkers had to borrow the cocktail glass or the sake bottle. The tumbler gave brown liquor its own symbol, and it was quickly adopted for bourbon, scotch, rye, rum, brandy and anything else served short. The official name describes the glass, but in practice almost everyone calls it the whiskey emoji, and many platforms reinforce that with amber liquid and ice.

Its tone is quieter than the cocktail glass. A tumbler suggests sitting down: a nightcap, a fireplace, a long conversation, a drink poured after a long day. People send it with a sigh to mean they need something strong, or to describe a calm evening alone. It also features in toasts at weddings, wakes and reunions, where a raised glass of whiskey carries a more serious, reflective feel than champagne.

Because the glass can also hold a shot, 🥃 does double duty in party contexts. Rows of tumblers can mean a round of shots at a birthday or bachelor party. Bartenders use it for spirit-forward cocktails like the old fashioned, which is served in a rocks glass. Distilleries, whiskey clubs and tasting accounts tag their posts with it, and gift guides for Father's Day lean on it heavily.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It signals winding down or a need for a strong drink. “Long day 🥃” needs no explanation, and “🥃?” is an invitation to a bar with a quieter, older crowd than a club. Among friends it can also announce shots: several tumblers in a row usually mean the night is about to get louder.

contexts.label: In captions
contexts.body: Whiskey tastings, distillery tours, cigar lounges and home bar setups are captioned with 🥃. Cocktail creators use it for old fashioneds, negronis and other drinks served over a big ice cube. It sits comfortably next to a fireplace photo or a cabin weekend, and bourbon fans pair it with references to Kentucky.

contexts.label: On holidays and occasions
contexts.body: Father's Day posts and gift ideas use it constantly, along with retirement parties and milestone birthdays. St. Patrick's Day brings it out for Irish whiskey, and Burns Night celebrations in Scotland feature scotch. At memorials, a raised 🥃 can mean a toast to someone who has died, a respectful use quite different from party shots.

confusedWith.difference: 🍸 is a stemmed martini glass and suggests bars, mixed drinks and a dressed-up night. 🥃 is a short glass for spirits served neat, on ice or as shots.
🥤 is a disposable cup with a lid and straw, used for soda, smoothies and fast food. It has nothing to do with alcohol, though both are short drink containers.
🍶 is a ceramic sake bottle with a small cup, tied to Japanese restaurants. People used it as a makeshift liquor emoji before 🥃 existed, but now 🥃 is the standard for whiskey.

avoid: Avoid sending it to someone who is sober or in recovery as a casual invitation.
Do not use it in contexts involving minors or driving, where it signals approval of drinking.
Skip party-style rows of shots in a memorial thread; a single glass reads as respectful, a string reads as celebration.
design: A short, straight-sided glass with a thick base, partly filled with amber liquid that reads as whiskey. Many designs include one or two ice cubes, and the glass is usually shown slightly from above so the liquid surface is visible. Variation between platforms is mostly in the shade of brown and whether ice is present; the rocks-glass shape is consistent.

faqs.a: Yes, 🥃 is the closest thing. Its official name is tumbler glass, but the amber drink and short glass make it the standard emoji for whiskey, bourbon and scotch, as well as other spirits served neat or on ice.
It can. Shot is one of its official tags, and several in a row usually mean a round of shots. A single tumbler in a relaxed context is more likely a slow drink, like whiskey on the rocks.

faqs.q: What does 🥃 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: Usually that he is drinking, relaxing or inviting you for a drink. In a dating context, suggesting whiskey at a bar is a common low-key date idea. It carries no innuendo on its own.

faqs.q: When was the tumbler glass emoji added?
faqs.a: 🥃 was added in 2016, much later than the beer, wine and cocktail emojis, which date back to the original Japanese sets. Before then, people improvised with 🍸 or 🍶.
